items.relation: technique-level bans to elicit new strategies, scored behaviourally; no execution-order check of whether a banned technique returns under a new name

items.title: Compact Constraint Encoding for LLM Code Generation (Tang 2026)
items.quote: counter-intuitive constraints opposing model defaults fail at 10--100%, while conventional constraints achieve 99%+ compliance regardless of encoding.
items.relation: rule-based constraint compliance by constraint type (implementation priors); not mechanism-level vs name-level compliance

items.title: The Invisible Lottery: How Subtle Cues Steer Algorithm Choice in LLM Code Generation
items.quote: Incidental prompt cues, meaning contextual words or metadata outside the task specification, can steer which algorithm the model selects, even when all outputs pass the same tests.
items.relation: algorithm-family shifts under incidental cues; no prohibitions, no runtime expansion-order audit

predictions.R6: the rename hypothesis: a prompt that bans a model's path-search repertoire by NAME is obeyed on names (lexically) but not on mechanisms: the banned expansion orders come back under new names

N1.claim: Across the 10 retraced five-name-ban configurations, lexical compliance exceeds mechanistic compliance (gap = lex - mech, among traceable programs).
N1.primary: equal-weight mean of the 10 per-configuration gaps (95% configuration-cluster bootstrap, 10,000 resamples); program-weighted pooled gap beside it
N1.supported: pooled gap >= 0.3 AND gap > 0 in >= 7/10 configurations
N1.tests: per configuration: 2x2 lex x mech, Newcombe paired interval (method 10), exact McNemar on the discordant cells
sensitivities: untraceable counted as compliant (lower bound) and as non-compliant (upper bound)

N2.claim: Qwen3-32B-thinking's correct NAME-level survivors of the five-name ban mostly run a banned coarse order class.
N2.pool: iteration-8 screen 17 + held-out 21 + new A k=5 (W1-W3) + new A held-out
N2.supported: share in a banned coarse order class >= 0.6 (Wilson CI reported)
readings: (b) survivors whose name-level identity is not BFS order by definition (excluding unit Dijkstra, FIFO SPFA, wavefront/flood fill, uniform-cost search)
N2-adj: observed share minus the uniform-over-non-banned-catalogue null (0.6 coarse, 0.2 fine), Wilson interval shifted; the text states whether the share exceeds the null
N2.by_source: iteration-8 rows (cap 9,728) vs new rows (cap 12,288) reported separately

N3.claim: Under cumulative bans B_k = first k of [BFS, DFS, IDDFS, A*, greedy] on Qwen3-32B thinking, mechanistic compliance falls with k while lexical compliance stays high.
criteria: k=1: lexical and mechanistic compliance both >= 0.7
Jonckheere-Terpstra one-sided (decreasing in k) on binary mechanistic compliance over the 5 ordered groups: Monte-Carlo exact p (100,000 permutations) < 0.05; Cochran-Armitage beside
N3.denominators: among completed programs (primary) and over all samples
sensitivities: fine classes (e.g. greedy at k=4 is compliant)

N3-D.claim: exploratory: a name-free described five-mechanism ban vs the named k=5 cell
N3-D.direction: under R6, mechanistic compliance OR violation (banned class) rises relative to the named k=5 cell (unpaired Newcombe)
measures: lexical use of any banned name

N5.claim: secondary: across the literal set and six rotated five-name sets, name-level survivors sit mechanistically CLOSER to the banned set (Dm < 0) and NAME-wise FARTHER from it (Dn > 0) than the non-banned ...
N5.supported: >= 5 of 7 sets (or of the defined sets, with >= 4 defined) with Dm < 0 AND Dn > 0
N5.tests: exact algorithm-level permutation per set; binomial sign test over sets (p0 = 0.25 joint, 0.5 per component)

n3d_descriptions.bfs: a search that explores cells in rings of increasing step count from the start, keeping discovered cells in a first-in-first-out line
n3d_descriptions.dfs: a search that follows one branch as far as it can go before backing up to the last fork, keeping discovered cells in a last-in-first-out pile
n3d_descriptions.iddfs: a search that repeats a branch-following search from the start with a step limit that grows by one each round
n3d_descriptions.astar: a search that always expands the open cell with the smallest sum of steps taken so far plus an estimate of the steps remaining to the goal
n3d_descriptions.gbfs: a search that always expands the open cell with the smallest estimate of the steps remaining to the goal, ignoring the steps taken so far
